newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 27.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 27.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HANOVER - Travel group Touristik Union International (TUI) has invited four agencies to present ideas for a possible advertising campaign. Aside from Springer & Jacoby, which now holds the account, TUI says it will view presentations from BBDO, TBWA and Menzel Nolte Heinemann. A decision is expected in a few weeks. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Taste!, an ad agency based in Neu-Isenburg that specialises in food and drink, says it expects 10-percent growth in 1997. It made a modest 5.5 million marks ($3.2 million) in income in 1996. It has also named Theo Probst-Bartolomee its creative director. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG says it has signed a preliminary interconnection agreement with Viag Interkom GmbH that it expects to finalise before the end of the year. The deal with the joint venture of Viag and British Telecom ensures Viag Interkom will be able to use Telekom's monopoly infrastructure to gain access to customers in local networks when markets are deregulated next year. Telekom also tells shareholders its online service is growing strongly and it expects to notch up its 1.5 millionth customer for the service any day now. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - North Rhine-Westphalia state Economics Minister Wolfgang Clement says he expects Telekom to be handed exclusive control over the technical platform to be used for access to digital cable television. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - Commercial TV group RTL is to be build a 500- square-metre restaurant in the centre of its home town of Cologne during the second half of the year. The restaurant, to be decked out with RTL sets and other paraphenalia, is to be the first of other such ventures across Germany. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - German news agency Deutsche-Presse-Agentur is to pay a dividend for the first time in its 48-year history to the 200 publishers and broadcast firms that are its owners. (Die Welt)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

COLOGNE - Lufthansa says it will end the first half of 1997 with profits higher than in same periods for 1995 and 1996 periods due to strong passenger growth and cost-cutting at the German airline. Lufthansa says it wants to strengthen its relationship with travel group NUR, a unit of retail group Karstadt, and to sell its 18-percent stake in travel and transport group Hapag Lloyd AG. "The leadership of (its tour unit) Condor and NUR are holding talks over a closer working relationship," Lufthansa Chairman Juergen Weber said. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - The HDE German retailers' association lashes out at the "stack 'em high, sell 'em cheap" large retail outlets finally making an appearance in Germany, arguing that consumers should boycott the American-style centres because they will ultimately lead to a fall in competition. Manufacturers use the stores to offer brand-name goods at prices 30 to 50 percent below downtown rates in mainly out-of-town locations, such as the 50,000 square meter megastore planned for Zweibrucken in western Germany. "Manufacturers, usually partners of retailers, are leaving their usual place in the chain and emerging as competitors. Worse, they are offering discounts," HDE President Holger Wenzel says. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Shell is looking to take over the German petrol station chain of Norway's Statoil, which has some 48 outlets in the former Communist-controlled east German states. The deal will mean Shell will have a total 241 outlets in the region. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Susanne Hoffmann is to take over marketing of the Mueller brand, owned by the dairy group Alois Mueller. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Hubert Burda takes over from Werner Hippe as President of the VDZ federation of German newspaper publishers. (Kress)
